subject: social-studies
title: Water Supply: From Rain to Tap, Stage by Stage
objectives: Explain Singapore's water supply in stages: rain collected in a reservoir, raw water drawn to the treatment works, treatment cleaning stage by stage, cleaned water stored and piped to home taps
Name what happens to the water at each stage and why the cleanliness bar climbs only during treatment
Explain why collected water is raw water, not tap water, until treatment stages have removed dirt and germs

definitions.meaning: A large store where rain that falls on the catchment is collected and kept as raw water at the start of the supply chain.
Water that has been collected but not yet treated: reservoir water is raw water, still carrying dirt and germs, and not safe to drink.
The place the raw water is drawn to, where treatment stages clean the water before it is stored and piped to homes.
The cleaning of the water stage by stage at the treatment works - dirt settles and sinks, germs are trapped and removed, and the cleanliness bar climbs at every stage.
The cleaned water at the end of the chain: only water that has been treated, then stored and piped to home taps, is tap water safe to drink.
The land where the rain falls and drains into the reservoir to be collected.

mechanismSteps: Stage 1: rain is collected in a reservoir - rain falls on the catchment, the reservoir stores it as raw water that still carries dirt and germs, and the cleanliness bar is low (s1).
Stage 2: raw water is drawn to the treatment works - pipes carry the raw water from the reservoir to the treatment works, and the bar barely moves because moving the water does not clean it (s2).
Stage 3: treatment cleans the water, stage by stage - dirt settles and sinks, germs are trapped and removed, and the cleanliness bar climbs 70 to 140 to 210 to 280 as each stage removes more (s3).
Stage 4: clean water is stored and piped to home taps - only the cleaned water is stored and piped to homes, the bar is full, and the shortcut of drinking from the reservoir is corrected (s4).
workedExample: Work through the whole journey in order. Stage 1 (s1): rain falls on the catchment and is collected in a reservoir, stored as raw water that is not yet safe to drink. Stage 2 (s2): the raw water is drawn from the reservoir through pipes to the treatment works, and moving it does not clean it. Stage 3 (s3): at the treatment works the water is cleaned stage by stage - dirt settles and sinks, germs are trapped and removed - and the cleanliness bar climbs 70 to 140 to 210 to 280. Stage 4 (s4): the cleaned water is stored and piped to home taps. At every stage the order is the same: reservoir, treatment works, cleaned and stored, home taps, and what makes the water safe is the treatment stages in between.

trap.misconception: Tap water is clean as soon as it is collected, because rainwater and reservoir water are already safe to drink.
trap.explanation: The slip: Rain looks clean as it falls and reservoir water looks clear in photographs, so it is easy to assume collected water is already safe to drink with no further steps. The fix: Collected water is raw water, not tap water: it is drawn from the reservoir to the treatment works, where treatment stages remove dirt and germs step by step, and only the cleaned water is stored and piped to home taps. In class, replay scene 3: freeze at each treatment tank and ask what that stage removes and how far the cleanliness bar climbs, then run scene 4 and contrast the treated route to the taps with the shortcut straight from the reservoir.
